rmt-2007-calc-01.title: Series
rmt-2007-calc-01.body:
$-1+\cos x=-\frac{x^2}2+O(x^4)$ and the denominator is $3x^2(1+\frac43x)$, so the quotient tends to $-\frac{1/2}{3}=-\frac16$.

**Answer: $-\frac16$**

rmt-2007-calc-02.title: Slope two ways
rmt-2007-calc-02.body:
The tangent slope at $x=a$ is $3a^2+3$; the line through the origin and $(a,b)$ has slope $\frac ba=\frac{a^3+3a+1}a$. Equate: $3a^3+3a=a^3+3a+1$, so $2a^3=1$, $a=\frac1{\sqrt[3]2}=\frac{\sqrt[3]4}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt[3]4}2$**

rmt-2007-calc-03.title: Integrate the speed
rmt-2007-calc-03.body:
The water amount is proportional to $t$, so the speed is $v=\frac kt$. The distance in the first hour of recording is $k\ln\frac{\tau+1}\tau$, in the second $k\ln\frac{\tau+2}{\tau+1}$. The condition gives $\ln\frac{\tau+1}\tau=2\ln\frac{\tau+2}{\tau+1}$, so $\frac{\tau+1}\tau=\left(\frac{\tau+2}{\tau+1}\right)^2$, i.e. $(\tau+1)^3=\tau(\tau+2)^2$.

Expanding, $\tau^3+3\tau^2+3\tau+1=\tau^3+4\tau^2+4\tau$, so $\tau^2+\tau-1=0$ and $\tau=\frac{\sqrt5-1}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt5-1}2$ hours**

rmt-2007-calc-04.title: Evaluate and sum
rmt-2007-calc-04.body:
For odd $m$, $I(m)=\left[-\frac{\cos mx}m\right]_0^\pi=\frac2m$. Every $5^n$ is odd, so the sum is $\sum_{n\ge0}\frac2{5^n}=\frac2{1-1/5}=\frac52$.

**Answer: $\frac52$**

rmt-2007-calc-06.title: Condition on A
rmt-2007-calc-06.body:
By symmetry take $A=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ with $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$. The other two vertices are $(\cos\theta,y_B)$ and $(x_B,\sin\theta)$. They lie in the disk exactly when $|y_B|\le\sin\theta$ and $|x_B|\le\cos\theta$ (the rectangle is then inside since the disk is convex). So $B$ must lie in a rectangle of area $4\sin\theta\cos\theta=2\sin2\theta$, and the probability for this $A$ is $\frac{2\sin2\theta}{\pi}$.

Averaging over $\theta$ uniform on $[0,\frac\pi2]$: $\frac2\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{2\sin2\theta}\pi\,d\theta=\frac2\pi\cdot\frac2\pi\cdot1=\frac4{\pi^2}$.

**Answer: $\frac4{\pi^2}$**

rmt-2007-calc-07.title: Disk method
rmt-2007-calc-07.body:
The balloon is the solid of revolution about the $x$-axis for $0\le x\le2$: $V=\pi\int_0^2(2x-x^2)e^{-x}\,dx$. Since $\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^2e^{-x}\right)=(2x-x^2)e^{-x}$, $V=\pi\left[x^2e^{-x}\right]_0^2=\frac{4\pi}{e^2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{4\pi}{e^2}$**

rmt-2007-calc-08.title: Two-step optimisation
rmt-2007-calc-08.body:
Coffee takes $\frac c{12}$ hours a day, so he does math for $24-s-\frac c{12}$ hours and proves $T=(s+\ln c)\left(24-s-\frac c{12}\right)$ theorems.

Let $u=s+\ln c$ and $v=24-s-\frac c{12}$. Then $u+v=24+\ln c-\frac c{12}$ does not depend on $s$, and for a fixed sum the product $uv$ is largest when $u=v$ (this needs $s=12-\frac c{24}-\frac12\ln c\ge0$, true near the optimum), giving $T=\frac14\left(24+\ln c-\frac c{12}\right)^2$.

Maximise $g(c)=\ln c-\frac c{12}$: $g'(c)=\frac1c-\frac1{12}=0$ gives $c=12$, a maximum since $g''<0$.

**Answer: 12 cups**

rmt-2007-calc-09.title: Harmonic numbers
rmt-2007-calc-09.body:
The sum is $H_{2n}-H_n$ and $H_m=\ln m+\gamma+o(1)$, so the difference tends to $\ln2n-\ln n=\ln2$.

**Answer: $\ln2$**

rmt-2007-calc-10.title: Integrate, then expand
rmt-2007-calc-10.body:
$\int\frac{x}{(x^2-1)^2}dx=-\frac1{2(x^2-1)}=\frac1{2(1-x^2)}=\frac12\sum_{k\ge0}x^{2k}$ (constant of integration dropped). Differentiating, $f(x)=\sum_{k\ge1}kx^{2k-1}=x+2x^3+3x^5+\cdots$. The $10^{\text{th}}$ nonzero term is $k=10$: $10x^{19}$.

**Answer: $10x^{19}$**
